title: Reproducible multi-language SDK releases, changelogs and signed artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a unified, reproducible release pipeline for the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that produces signed artifacts (PyPI wheels/sdist, npm tarballs, Go modules), machine-readable provenance attestations, and human-friendly changelogs. Motivation: reduce release toil, eliminate accidental unsigned publishes, and provide downstream consumers with verifiable provenance for compliance-sensitive customers. Scope: CI changes (GitHub Actions workflows and release runners), per-language packaging config (setuptools/poetry -> wheel/sdist; npm pack; Go module tag consistency), deterministic versioning (changelog-driven release notes + conventional commits optional), artifact signing (in-toto/SLSA attestation or cosign signatures), and example updates (streaming ergonomics and retry examples in each language). Out of scope: major SDK API surface changes. Non-goal: change public API except where strictly needed for ergonomics examples.
acceptance_criteria: Automated CI job that builds Python, TS, and Go artifacts on a release tag and stores artifacts in a reproducible artifact bucket
Signed artifacts published to test registries (Test PyPI / npm from staging / private Go module proxy) with verifiable signature attached
A machine-readable provenance file (SLSA-in-toto or comparable) is emitted for each build and archived alongside artifacts
Human-readable changelog is generated automatically from merged PRs and included in the release notes
Example apps demonstrating streaming ergonomics and retry strategies updated in each language repo and shipped with release examples
Security review performed and documented for signing key handling and CI secrets; KMS/HSM integration plan validated
tasks: Design signing approach: cosign vs in-toto attestation. (Decision: cosign for binaries + in-toto link metadata for source provenance)
Create GitHub Actions release workflow that runs matrix builds for py/ts/go and outputs deterministic artifact hashes
Add reproducible-build flags and lockfile snapshots for each language (pip-compile/poetry-lock, npm ci + package-lock, go mod tidy + vendor optional)
Wire CI to create a provenance/attestation JSON and upload to artifacts bucket (s3/gcs) with ACLs
Integrate KMS for signing keys; add key rotation plan and access control (secrets manager -> short-lived signing key per-run)
Publish process docs and a one-click checklist for engineering/sdks on Confluence + short video walkthrough
Update SDK examples to include streaming usage and retry backoff patterns; add e2e test against staging endpoint
Smoke tests post-publish that verify package integrity and signature verification for each registry
Add semantic-release or release-helper that assembles changelog from PR labels and commit messages
notes: Trade-offs considered: full SLSA 3 pipeline is ideal but heavier; MVP will target reproducible artifacts + cosign signatures + in-toto metadata to balance effort vs compliance
We will use GitHub Actions for consistency with existing infra; long-term we may backport to internal runners if needed for on-prem releases
Python packaging: prefer wheel + sdist with pinned build environment to ensure reproducible wheels (manylinux image with fixed pip/setuptools versions)
NPM: use npm ci and deterministic node container; ensure package-lock is respected. Consider npm sign later if registry support is required
Go: tag-to-module mapping must be enforced; add a release script that verifies 'go mod verify' and publishes to our proxy for QA
Key storage: initial plan uses HashiCorp Vault-backed signing key with short TTLs and audit logs; product security to approve
Changelog strategy: use PR labels 'feat|fix|chore|docs|perf' to drive sections; maintainers can edit before publish
Docs & examples: streaming ergonomic API patterns will be standardized across languages (async iterators in TS/Python, channel-style in Go)
Edge case: we need a fallback flow for emergency fixes where signing key path is unavailable — documented emergency publish SOP
